Water Heater Repair in Houston, TX: Who to Call

A water heater is plumbing in Texas, not heating and air conditioning. This guide explains who is licensed to repair or replace one in Houston, how to check that license, and what to do first when something looks or smells wrong.

Call (832) 662-4107 Check a plumber's license
  1. Home
  2. Water Heater Repair

If you searched for water heater repair in Houston, TX, here is the honest answer up front: Houston Air & Heating cannot help with it. The line only handles heating and air conditioning calls, and in Texas a water heater falls under plumbing, a separate licensed trade. What this page can do is point you to the right kind of professional, show you how to check that person's license in a couple of minutes, and walk through the safety steps that matter before anyone arrives.

The same caution applies if an HVAC company offers to swap your water heater. Some businesses hold both a heating and cooling license and a plumbing license, and that is fine. The point is to know which license the job needs and to see it before work begins.

Water heater safety in a Houston home

Most water heater trouble is an inconvenience. These situations are not, and they come before any repair call.

Gas smell near a gas water heater

Walk out of the house right away and take everyone with you. CenterPoint Energy, which supplies natural gas across much of the Houston area, says not to use switches, phones or anything that could spark on the way out and not to touch the meter or valves. From a safe distance, call 911 and CenterPoint's gas leak line at 888-876-5786.

Carbon monoxide alarm sounding

A gas water heater burns fuel and vents exhaust, just like a furnace. If a CO alarm goes off, or several people feel headachy, dizzy or sick at once, get everyone outside into fresh air and call 911. Do not go back in until responders say it is safe.

Hot water spraying or pouring out

Scalding water can burn in seconds. Keep children and pets back, stay clear of the relief valve outlet, and call a plumber. Do not plug or cap the relief pipe to stop the flow.

Water around an electric unit or outlet

Water and electricity together are dangerous. Stay out of standing water near an electric water heater or nearby outlets, and let a licensed professional deal with the wiring.

Why water heater repair in Houston is a plumber's job

Texas licenses plumbers through the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners under the Plumbing License Law in Chapter 1301 of the Occupations Code. The law's definition of plumbing reaches the appliances and piping that supply, distribute or circulate water or gas in a building, which is exactly what a tank or tankless water heater is. The board's rules also say that installing a gas-fueled water heater or cutting into fuel gas piping is not the kind of incidental plumbing that an unlicensed maintenance worker may do under the law's maintenance exemption.

Heating and air conditioning is a different license. TDLR issues Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractor licenses for heating, cooling and refrigeration work, and state law goes the other way too: a plumbing license alone does not let someone do air conditioning contracting. So an ACR license is the right thing to ask for when the furnace or AC fails, and a plumbing license is the right thing to ask for when the water heater does.

What this means when you call around

  • Ask for a plumbing license number, not just a business name or a heating and cooling license.
  • Ask whether a master plumber is responsible for the company's work. Texas requires a plumbing company that serves the public to have a Responsible Master Plumber.
  • Ask who pulls the permit if the tank is being replaced.
  • Ask for a written price before work starts, and whether haul-away of the old tank is included.

How to check a Texas plumber's license

The plumbing board runs a free Public License Search on its website. It takes a couple of minutes and shows far more than whether a license exists.

  1. Get the license number. Ask the plumber or company for it. Master Plumber license numbers start with the letter M.
  2. Open the TSBPE Public License Search at tsbpe.texas.gov and choose the plumbing license option.
  3. Enter the number without the letter. The board's instructions say to type the digits only.
  4. Open the record and read it. It shows whether the license is current, when it expires, endorsements, any disciplinary actions and whether a certificate of insurance is on file.
  5. For a company, check its Responsible Master Plumber as well, and confirm that person's license and insurance certificate.
  6. Save a screenshot of the record with your paperwork.

The board also offers a Find-a-Plumber tool on its website, which can help if you are starting from scratch.

Common water heater symptoms and what they often mean

This table is for describing the problem clearly to a plumber. It is not a repair guide: gas valves, burners, electric elements and wiring are for a licensed professional.

Water heater symptoms, what they may point to, and what a homeowner can safely do
What you noticeWhat it may point toSafe for you to do
No hot water from an electric heaterA tripped breaker, a failed heating element or thermostatReset the water heater breaker once; if it trips again, leave it off and call
No hot water from a gas heaterAn ignition or pilot problem, a gas supply issue or a failed controlCheck whether other gas appliances work; leave the burner area alone
Water dripping from the relief valve pipeA worn valve, water overheating, high household pressure or thermal expansionKeep clear of the outlet, never cap the pipe, call a plumber
Puddle at the base of the tankA leaking fitting, relief valve discharge or the tank itselfMove belongings away, note where the water seems to start, call a plumber
Water much hotter than usualA thermostat or control problemWarn the household about scalding and call; check the temperature at a faucet
Gas or rotten egg smellA possible gas leakLeave the house and call 911 and CenterPoint from outside

Replacing a water heater in the City of Houston

According to the Houston Permitting Center, a plumbing permit is required to replace or install a water heater inside city limits. The permit has to be obtained by a master plumber who has registered a state license with the City of Houston. For a single-family home no plan review is needed, but the work must pass an inspection, and the permit stays valid for 180 days. Because the plumber pulls the permit, ask whether it is included in the price you are quoted.

Those rules cover the City of Houston itself. Suburban cities and unincorporated areas set their own requirements, so if you live outside Houston city limits, ask the plumber which rules apply and check with your city's building department.

A safer setting while you wait

Keeping household hot water at a lower setting is a simple safety step. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission advises 120 degrees Fahrenheit or lower to help prevent scald burns. It suggests checking with a cooking thermometer under a faucet first thing in the morning rather than relying on the dial. If your water heater runs on gas and you are not sure how to adjust it, leave that to the plumber.

Common questions

Who do I call to repair a water heater in Houston?

Call a licensed plumber. In Texas, plumbing is licensed by the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners, and its Public License Search lets you confirm a plumber's license before work starts. Inside the City of Houston, a replacement also needs a plumbing permit pulled by a master plumber registered with the city.

Can an HVAC company do plumbing or fix my water heater?

Only if the company also holds a Texas plumbing license. An air conditioning and refrigeration license from TDLR covers heating and cooling work, while water heaters fall under the state plumbing law. Some businesses carry both licenses; ask for the plumbing license number and check it with the plumbing board.

Do I need a permit to replace a water heater in Houston?

Yes, inside City of Houston limits. The Houston Permitting Center says a plumbing permit is required to replace or install a water heater, the permit must be obtained by a master plumber registered with the city, and an inspection is required. Suburbs set their own rules, so check with your city if you live outside Houston.

Why is water dripping from the pipe on the side of my water heater?

That pipe usually comes from the temperature and pressure relief valve, a safety device that opens when the tank gets too hot or the pressure climbs too high. A drip can mean the valve is worn, the water is overheating or household water pressure is too high. Never cap or plug that pipe. Keep people away from hot discharge and call a plumber.

What temperature should my water heater be set to?

To help prevent scald burns, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission says to keep it at 120 degrees Fahrenheit or lower. It suggests checking the real temperature with a thermometer at a faucet rather than trusting the dial. On a gas water heater, have a plumber make adjustments if you are unsure.
